§3.5.4 Interactions

3.5.4 Interactions

3.6 More Information on the S-matrix

  • The 𝑆-matrix describes the interaction between particles in the system, and as previously seen, it is defined as

    ⟨𝑓|𝑆|𝑖⟩=𝟙+(2𝜋)4𝛿4(𝑝𝑓−𝑝𝑖)ℳ︁

  • This S-matrix is the primary goal of most calculations in quantum field theory (as it describes the interactions of the particles)

3.6.1 LSZ Reduction

  • The way to obtain the S-matrix from the Time-Ordered Product involves the LSZ Reduction Formula which is extremely important, and allows for the derivation of the extremely simple momentum-space Feynman Rules, which you will see later.

  • The LSZ reduction formula is as follows:

    ⟨𝑓|𝑆|𝑖⟩=[𝑖∫𝑑4𝑥1𝑒−𝑖𝑝1𝑥1(□+𝑚2)]⋯[𝑖∫𝑑4𝑥𝑛𝑒𝑖𝑝𝑛𝑥𝑛(□+𝑚2)]×⟨Ω|𝑇𝜙(𝑥1)𝜙(𝑥2)𝜙(𝑥3)…𝜙(𝑥𝑛)|Ω⟩

Definition 3.6.1.1 (LSZ Reduction).

The LSZ Reduction is a formula providing 𝑆- matrix elements from the time ordered product (in the ground state for the interacting theory Ω).

  • Additionally, this formula can allow for the calculation of transfer matrix elements ℳ︁, but it is more convenient to utilize Feynman diagrams derived from this formulation.

    • The cross sections are calculatable from this as well

  • This formula effectively deletes terms in the time ordered product except for those with poles of 1𝑝2−𝑚2

  • The ground state in the interacting theory, |Ω⟩ is a very inconvenient way to calculate, due to lack of knowledge about the ground state

3.6.1.1 Correlation Functions

  • A correlation function ⟨Ω|𝑇𝜙(𝑥1)⋯𝜙(𝑥𝑛)|Ω⟩ is the time ordered product of fields which appears in the LSZ reduction formula after the integrals

  • This is specifically used in the derivation of the LSZ reduction formula

3.6.1.2 Derivation of LSZ Reduction

  • Suppose that the initial state |𝑖⟩ and the final state |𝑓⟩ are of the form

    |𝑖⟩=2𝜔12𝜔2𝑎𝑝1†(−∞)𝑎𝑝2†(∞)|Ω⟩

    and

    |𝑓⟩=2𝜔1⋯2𝜔𝑗𝑎𝑝3†(∞)⋯𝑎𝑝𝑗†(∞)|Ω⟩
    • Additionally there is the constraint that |𝑖⟩≠|𝑓⟩ due to scattering happening.

  • The S-matrix element is then

    ⟨𝑓|𝑆|𝑖⟩=2𝑗2𝜔1⋯𝜔𝑛×⟨Ω|𝑎𝑝3(∞)⋯𝑎𝑝𝑗(∞)𝑎𝑝1†(−∞)𝑎𝑝2†(−∞)|Ω⟩
  • Now it is desirable to convert this to scalar fields, 𝜙

  • From quantization, they are defined by

    𝜙=∫d3𝑝(2𝜋)3(𝑎𝑝(𝑡)𝑒−𝑖𝑝𝑥+𝑎𝑝†(𝑡)𝑒𝑖𝑝𝑥)
3.6.1.2.1 Heisenberg picture to obtain operators

  • Consider the Heisenberg picture

    • 𝑎𝑝(𝑡)=𝑒𝑖𝐻(𝑡−𝑡0)𝑎𝑝(𝑡0)𝑒−𝑖𝐻(𝑡−𝑡0) and 𝜙(𝑥)=𝑒𝑖𝐻(𝑡−𝑡0)𝜙(𝒙,𝑡0)𝑒−𝑖𝐻(𝑡−𝑡0) via unitary time evolution

    • The only useful thing to know about 𝜙(𝑥,𝑡) and 𝑎𝑝(𝑡) is

      ⟨Ω|𝜙(𝒙,𝑡=±∞)|𝑝⟩=𝐶𝑒−𝑖𝒑⋅𝒙

  • A useful identity:

    𝑖∫d4𝑥𝑒𝑖𝑝𝑥(□+𝑚2)𝜙(𝑥)=2𝜔𝑝[𝑎𝑝(∞)−𝑎𝑝(−∞)]

    • Proof:

      𝑖∫d4𝑥(□+𝑚2)𝜙(𝑥)=𝑖∫d4𝑥𝑒𝑖𝑝𝑥(𝜕𝑡2−𝜕⃗𝑥2+𝑚2)𝜙=𝑖∫d4𝑥𝑒𝑖𝑝𝑥(𝜕𝑡2+𝑝⃗2+𝑚2)𝜙(𝑥)=𝑖∫d4𝑒𝑖𝑝𝑥(𝜕𝑡2+𝜔𝑝2)𝜙(𝑥)

      • Identity for proof:

        𝜕𝑡[𝑒𝑖𝑝𝑥(𝑖𝜕𝑡+𝜔𝑝)𝜙(𝑥)]=[𝑖𝜔𝑝𝑒𝑖𝑝𝑥(𝑖𝜕𝑡+𝜔𝑝)+𝑒𝑖𝑝𝑥(𝑖𝜕𝑡2+𝜔𝑝𝜕𝑡2)]𝜙(𝑥)=𝑖𝑒𝑖𝑝𝑥(𝜕𝑡2+𝜔2)𝜙(𝑥)

    • Putting this into the integral,

      𝑖∫d4𝑥𝑒𝑖𝑝𝑥(□+𝑚2)𝜙(𝑥)=∫d4𝑥𝜕𝑡[𝑒𝑖𝑝𝑥(𝑖𝜕𝑡+𝜔𝑝)𝜙(𝑥)]=∫d𝑡𝜕𝑡[𝑒𝑖𝜔𝑝𝑡∫d3𝑥𝑒−𝑖𝒑⋅𝒙(𝑖𝜕𝑡+𝜔𝑝)𝜙(𝑥)]
      • This is true for all 𝜙(𝑥)

    • Quantum Field Case:

      ∫d3𝑥𝑒−𝑖𝒑⋅𝒙(𝑖𝜕𝑡+𝜔𝑝)𝜙(𝑥)=∫d3𝑥𝑒−𝑖𝒑⋅𝒙(𝑖𝜕𝑡+𝜔𝑝)×∫d3𝑘(2𝜋)312𝜔𝑘(𝑎𝑘(𝑡)𝑒−𝑖𝑘𝑥𝑎𝑘†(𝑡)𝑒𝑖𝑘𝑥)=∫d3𝑘(2𝜋)3∫d3𝑥((𝜔𝑘+𝜔𝑝2𝜔𝑘)𝑎𝑘(𝑡)𝑒−𝑖𝑘𝑥𝑒−𝑖𝒑⋅𝒙+(−𝜔𝑘+𝜔𝑝2𝜔𝑘)𝑎𝑘†(𝑡)𝑒𝑖𝑘𝑥𝑒−𝑖𝒑⋅𝒙)

Note that

  • 𝜕𝑡𝑎𝑘(𝑡)=0 at 𝑡=±∞

  • The d3𝑥 integral enforces 𝜔𝑘=𝜔𝑝 via delta functions

  • Therefore, we get

    ∫d3𝑥𝑒−𝑖𝒑⋅𝒙(𝑖𝜕𝑡+𝜔𝑝)𝜙(𝑥)=2𝜔𝑝𝑎𝑝(𝑡)𝑒−𝑖𝜔𝑝𝑡

  • This implies

    𝑖∫d4𝑥𝑒𝑖𝑝𝑥(□+𝑚2)𝜙(𝑥)=∫d𝑡𝜕𝑡((𝑒𝑖𝜔𝑝𝑡)(2𝜔𝑝𝑎𝑝(𝑡)𝑒−𝑖𝜔𝑝𝑡))=2𝜔𝑝[𝑎𝑝(∞)−𝑎𝑝(−∞)]

    as desired

3.6.1.2.2 S matrix element computing

  • Now we can compute

    ⟨𝑓|𝑆|𝑖⟩=2𝑗2𝜔1𝜔2…𝜔𝑗×⟨Ω|𝑎𝑝3(∞)…𝑎𝑝𝑗(∞)𝑎𝑝1†(−∞)𝑎𝑝2†(−∞)|Ω⟩

Definition 3.6.1.2.2.1 (Time Ordered Product).

  • The time ordered product 𝑇𝒪︁(𝑥1)𝒪︁(𝑥2)…𝒪︁(𝑥𝑛) picks up the operators 𝒪︁ and literally places them so that they are correctly ordered in time. This is the only thing that the operator does, as it keeps the products there.

  • Notice that

    ⟨𝑓|𝑆|𝑖⟩=2𝑗𝜔1…𝜔𝑗⟨Ω|𝑇[𝑎𝑝3(∞)−𝑎𝑝3(−∞)]⋯[𝑎𝑝𝑗(∞)−𝑎𝑝𝑗(−∞)]×[𝑎𝑝1†(−∞)−𝑎𝑝1†(∞)][𝑎𝑝2†(−∞)−𝑎𝑝2†(∞)]|Ω⟩

  • Therefore, we have the LSZ Reduction Formula

    ⟨𝑝3⋯𝑝𝑗|𝑆|𝑝1𝑝2⟩=[𝑖∫d4𝑥1𝑒−𝑖𝑝1𝑥1(□1+𝑚2)]×⋯×[𝑖∫d4𝑥𝑗𝑒𝑖𝑝𝑗𝑥𝑗(□𝑗+𝑚2)]×⟨Ω|𝑇𝜙(𝑥1)𝜙(𝑥2)…𝜙(𝑥𝑗)|Ω⟩
3.6.1.3 LSZ For Operators

  • The LSZ Reduction formula is relatively powerful, as it applies for all operators 𝒪︁𝑗

  • This implies that

    ⟨𝑝3⋯𝑝𝑗|𝑆|𝑝1𝑝2⟩=[𝑖∫d4𝑥1𝑒−𝑖𝑝1𝑥1(□1+𝑚2)]×⋯×[𝑖∫d4𝑥𝑗𝑒𝑖𝑝𝑗𝑥𝑗(□𝑗+𝑚2)]×⟨Ω|𝑇𝒪︁1(𝑥1)…𝒪︁𝑗(𝑥𝑗)|Ω⟩
